India’s real GDP growth has been reported at 7.8% in Q1 FY 2026-27 (April–June 2026), making it a major current affairs topic for UPSC Mains 2027 and other competitive examinations. But does a high GDP growth rate automatically mean that the Indian economy is becoming stronger?

In this UPSC Mains 2027 Live Brainstorming Session, we will go beyond the headline number and understand the bigger economic picture. The discussion focuses on India GDP Growth, Indian Economy, GDP Data, Economic Growth, Investment, Consumption, Manufacturing, Services, Employment and Inclusive Growth from a Mains-oriented perspective.

The latest official data shows that India’s real GDP grew by 7.8%, while real GVA recorded 8.2% growth in Q1 FY 2026-27. Investment and domestic demand also remain important parts of the growth story.

👉 What is driving India’s GDP growth?
👉 Is growth broad-based and sustainable?
👉 What is the role of manufacturing and services?
👉 How do investment and consumption contribute to growth?
👉 Can high GDP growth translate into better employment and inclusive development?
👉 What are the challenges in measuring India’s GDP accurately?

This session will help you convert a current economic event into a strong UPSC Mains answer, especially for GS Paper 3 – Indian Economy.

 UPSC CSE 2027 | UPSC Mains | GS 3 | Indian Economy | Current Affairs | Answer Writing | Essay Preparation

Watch till the end and learn how to use the latest GDP data effectively in your Mains answers.

snippet.description:
Benzene structure and stability is a crucial topic in Class 12 Chemistry Chapter 20 for Intermediate/FSc students. This comprehensive video explains the unique structure of benzene, its resonance forms, and why benzene is exceptionally stable despite having multiple double bonds.

In this lesson, you will learn:
• The molecular formula and structural formula of benzene
• How benzene exhibits resonance between two Kekulé structures

Pancreas and Adrenal Glands | Class 12 Biology Chapter 16 Complete Guide

This comprehensive video covers the structure, function, and hormonal regulation of the pancreas and adrenal glands—two critical endocrine organs in the human body. Designed for Class 12 (FSc Part 2) students following the FBISE and Punjab Board curriculum, this lesson explains how these glands maintain metabolic balance and respond to stress.

📚 WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
✓ Pancreatic structure and the islets of Langerhans
✓ Insulin and glucagon: regulation of blood glucose
✓ Adrenal cortex and medulla: hormones and functions
✓ Adrenaline and cortisol: role in stress response
✓ Clinical significance and disorders (diabetes, Addison's disease)
✓ Exam-focused key concepts for FBISE, Punjab, Sindh, and all Pakistani boards

The pancreas serves dual roles as both an endocrine and exocrine gland, while the adrenal glands sit atop the kidneys and coordinate critical body functions. Understanding these glands is essential for your Intermediate Biology exams and competitive tests.

This video follows the PCTB textbook and National Curriculum of Pakistan, making it perfect for all Pakistani students in Class 12, whether you're studying from Punjab, Sindh, KPK, Balochistan, or AJK boards.

✅ KEY TOPICS COVERED:
- Pancreatic hormones (insulin, glucagon, somatostatin)
- Blood glucose homeostasis
- Adrenal cortex hormones (glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids)
- Adrenal medulla and catecholamines
- Hormonal coordination and feedback mechanisms
- Common disorders and their management

Antiderivatives and indefinite integrals form the foundation of integral calculus and are essential topics in Class 12 Mathematics. This comprehensive video explains the fundamental concepts, techniques, and applications of finding antiderivatives and solving indefinite integrals.

In this lesson, you'll learn:
• The definition and properties of antiderivatives
• How to find indefinite integrals using standard integration formulas
• Integration by substitution method
• Integration by parts technique
• Solving real-world problems involving integration

This topic is crucial for students preparing for their FSc Part 2, Intermediate, and HSSC examinations under FBISE, Punjab Board (BISE Lahore, Rawalpindi, Multan, Faisalabad), Sindh Board, and other Pakistani educational boards. The PCTB textbook and National Curriculum of Pakistan emphasize mastering antiderivatives as a key skill for success in calculus.
